Check demo more: kept 8s required mirror-of-same-row 5. But is it really mirrored or just aligned? Both gave same result for cols 0-11 / 13-24 alignment (widths equal 12 each). Actually I used inp[r][13+c], no mirror. Good — simple per-row overlay.
def f(M):
    H,W=M.shape; res=np.zeros((H,W),int)
    # find separator lines: full row/col of a distinct color
    sep=None
    for r in range(H):
        if len(set(M[r]))==1 and M[r][0] not in (0,): sep=('h',r); break
    if sep is None:
        for c in range(W):
            if len({M[r][c] for r in range(H)})==1 and M[0][c] not in (0,): sep=('v',c); break
    if sep[0]=='v': s=sep[1]
    else: s=sep[1]; swap=True  # vertical stack: compare rows
    # determine which half contains "noise" pattern color vs other half
    # general: keep cells of dominant non-zero color in first half where second half has its own color at same index
    A=B=None
    if sep[0]=='v':
        A,B=M[:,:s],M[:,s+1:]
    else:
        A,B=M[:s],M[s+1:]
    ca=[x for x in set(A.flat) if x!=0 and sum(1 for v in A.flat if v==x)==max(sum(1 for v in A.flat if v==x) for x in set(A.flat)-{0})]
    cb=[x for x in set(B.flat) if x!=0]
